extracted.intended_audience: SEC disclosure lawyers / corporate securities counsel preparing MD&A
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing the Management’s Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) section of SEC periodic reports and registration statements, focusing on readability, Item 303 requirements, interplay with other disclosures, and common best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layered Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting layered disclosure, whereby the MD&A is ordered with the more important themes or highlights set forth at the beginning of the disclosure, with additional detail to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC Staff (including in its 2003 MD&A interpretative release) has advocated layered disclosure and it will enhance readability. Layered disclosure is facilitated by the inclusion of an executive summary at the beginning of the MD&A (an approach followed by some, but not all, registrants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Readability Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use headings, bullet points, and plain English to improve readability of the MD&A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve readability by using headings, bullet points, and a plain English drafting approach. Enhance readability by cross-referencing (rather than repeating) discussions elsewhere in the periodic report or (for Form 10-Q MD&A) disclosures in the Form 10-K, to the extent those disclosures do not require updating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 303 Requirement to Disclose Material Trends
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A must provide an analysis of known material trends, uncertainties and other events impacting a registrant’s results of operations, liquidity or capital resources (core Item 303 obligation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice varies on including forward‑looking statements in MD&A. Registrants may be cautious about expansive forward‑looking disclosure out of liability concerns, but countervailing considerations include usefulness to investors and potential exposure for failing to disclose known trends (e.g., Rule 10b‑5 private claims and SEC civil actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Trends Disclosure on Future Periodic Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosing material trends in MD&A may create an obligation to update that disclosure in subsequent periodic reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering whether to disclose a trend, registrants should be mindful that including such trends disclosure in the MD&A may, in certain circumstances, create the need to update (and continue) such disclosure in the next periodic report rather than simply deleting it in the next succeeding periodic report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of Trends Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a trend should be disclosed in the MD&A or in financial statement footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that the PSLRA safe harbor for forward‑looking statements (when accompanied by meaningful cautionary language) applies to disclosures in the MD&A but does not apply to financial statement footnote disclosures; this difference can affect where to place forward‑looking trend information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction between MD&A and Risk Factors Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether MD&A disclosure necessitates corresponding revisions to risk factors in the Form 10‑K or updates to risk factors in a Form 10‑Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting MD&A, disclosure counsel should consider whether any MD&A content also gives rise to a need (for Form 10‑K MD&A) to revise risk factors in the Form 10‑K or (for Form 10‑Q MD&A) to update risk factors for the Form 10‑Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of Factors Impacting Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing drivers of results, consider whether to quantify the impact of those trends during the applicable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure counsel should consider not only whether particular drivers materially impacted performance, but also whether it is helpful or necessary to quantify the impact to provide a clearer picture of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑GAAP Financial Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how extensively to include non‑GAAP financial measures in periodic reports versus earnings releases, and ensure compliance with SEC rules and Staff guidance when non‑GAAP measures are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many registrants include less extensive non‑GAAP disclosure in periodic reports than in earnings releases. If non‑GAAP disclosures are included in MD&A, counsel should closely review SEC rules and Staff guidance—particularly the requirement to provide equal or greater prominence to GAAP financial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Earnings Release Disclosure Package for Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistency between the periodic report MD&A and other investor communications such as the earnings release, earnings call transcript, and investor presentation deck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure counsel should review earnings release, earnings call transcript and (if applicable) earnings deck for consistency with the periodic report. The SEC Staff reviews earnings releases and earnings call transcripts, and material inconsistencies can trigger SEC comments. The Q&A portion of an earnings call may also reveal the most important issues and trends from analysts' perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑Period Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of events after the period end that may need disclosure because MD&A speaks as of the date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure counsel should consider the potential need to disclose events arising after the end of a quarter, even if they do not impact that quarter's results or require footnote disclosure (except in a subsequent events footnote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Peer Company Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodically review MD&A disclosures and SEC comment letters of peer companies to identify Staff focus areas and issues relevant to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be benefit in periodically reviewing peer company MD&A and peer SEC comment letters to assess areas of focus of the SEC Staff which may also be relevant to the registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose critical accounting policies and estimates in MD&A (or by cross‑reference), typically addressing a subset of accounting policies and explaining why they could be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most registrants will disclose critical accounting policies and estimates, commonly addressing three to five items (a subset of policies discussed in the financial statement footnotes). When doing so, provide an analysis as to why the impact of these critical accounting policies could be material. Cross‑referencing to the Form 10‑K is sometimes used.
